account: Rainforest Connection (RFCx), a US non-profit founded by Topher White, deploys solar-powered “Guardian” acoustic sensors. In its own words, they use “sound & artificial intelligence” to track chainsaws, vehicle engines, hunting dogs and gunshots. They send real-time alerts to a mobile app so that “an agent nearby” can respond. RFCx states that it has protected over 726,000 hectares (impact page) or 750,000 hectares (guardian page) across 8,662+ projects in 137 countries. At a KKI Warsi press conference reported by Antara on 16 July 2020, Warsi said that the first 12 Guardian units went up in July 2019 in Sirukam and other nagari forests. In August 2019, a Guardian alert led the Sirukam patrol to a logger, who was caught and then escaped. Warsi counted 12 chainsaw alerts from sensors at 17 sites, and it said that not all of them were illegal. A Thomson Reuters Foundation report published by The Straits Times on 11 February 2021 is the one independent account. It is from Solok regency, West Sumatra, Indonesia, where 27 Guardian sensors had been installed more than a year earlier. Audio streams are analyzed by AI trained to pick out chainsaw sounds, and an alert goes to community patrols. Patroller Jasrialdi said that logging “has totally stopped” in the area. The head of West Sumatra's forestry department, Yozarwardi Usama Putra, said that he would like to expand the “early-warning system”. The same report attributes the decline in logging to a wider enforcement crackdown as well. It reports that about 200 of Sirukam's 6,000 residents had worked in illegal logging. It reports that one former logger quit in 2018, before the sensors, because of the crackdown. It says that RFCx planned to collect data for peer review to prove that the system curbs logging. No park authority, ministry or court document records an alert that led to an interception.

ai_role.statement: RFCx's own pages describe AI classification of streamed audio generating app alerts for responders. The 2021 Reuters report confirms the mechanism at the Solok site: AI picks out chainsaw sounds and patrols are alerted. It quotes a patroller that logging stopped, while also crediting a government enforcement crackdown. Apart from that single news item, only the maker's account is among the sources. No park authority, ministry or court record of an AI-triggered interception was found. RFCx itself said in 2021 that peer-review data to prove the effect was still being collected.

fields.account: Rainforest Connection (RFCx), a US non-profit founded by Topher White, deploys solar-powered “Guardian” acoustic sensors. In its own words, they use “sound & artificial intelligence” to track chainsaws, vehicle engines, hunting dogs and gunshots. They send real-time alerts to a mobile app so that “an agent nearby” can respond. RFCx states that it has protected over 726,000 hectares (impact page) or 750,000 hectares (guardian page) across 8,662+ projects in 137 countries. At a KKI Warsi press conference reported by Antara on 16 July 2020, Warsi said that the first 12 Guardian units went up in July 2019 in Sirukam and other nagari forests. In August 2019, a Guardian alert led the Sirukam patrol to a logger, who was caught and then escaped. Warsi counted 12 chainsaw alerts from sensors at 17 sites, and it said that not all of them were illegal. A Thomson Reuters Foundation report published by The Straits Times on 11 February 2021 is the one independent account. It is from Solok regency, West Sumatra, Indonesia, where 27 Guardian sensors had been installed more than a year earlier. Audio streams are analyzed by AI trained to pick out chainsaw sounds, and an alert goes to community patrols. Patroller Jasrialdi said that logging “has totally stopped” in the area. The head of West Sumatra's forestry department, Yozarwardi Usama Putra, said that he would like to expand the “early-warning system”. The same report attributes the decline in logging to a wider enforcement crackdown as well. It reports that about 200 of Sirukam's 6,000 residents had worked in illegal logging. It reports that one former logger quit in 2018, before the sensors, because of the crackdown. It says that RFCx planned to collect data for peer review to prove that the system curbs logging. No park authority, ministry or court document records an alert that led to an interception.
fields.summary: Rainforest Connection's Guardian sensors use AI to detect chainsaws and alert patrols; in West Sumatra an alert led a patrol to a logger in August 2019, and a patroller said that logging stopped.

purpose: Real-time acoustic detection of illegal logging and poaching sounds so that rangers or community patrols can respond; the reported benefit is the intended one.

ratings.reason: Patrollers in Sirukam say that alerts let them go straight to a chainsaw's location, and local monitors told Reuters that the system made their work easier. The gain is speed of response; the one dated interception, in August 2019, ended with the logger escaping.

A patroller told Reuters that logging in the Sirukam area had stopped. The same report credits a wider enforcement crackdown, and a former logger quit in 2018, before the sensors, so no source ties the change to the alerts.
